title: Chapter 226: Believe Me
html:
Dressed in the bloodstained doctor’s coat and wearing the skin mask, Chen Ge opened the wooden panels. Ten minutes have passed without a single scream. It looks like they’ve adjusted to the Third Sick Hall.

Chen Ge felt that he had become too softhearted. Afraid the opening scares might overwhelm the visitors, he had given them a ten-minute head start.

They should have found the tape recorder. Things will be a little more difficult from now on.

Chen Ge descended the darkened stairs. At the bottom, he glanced down the left corridor. Not a single mannequin stood outside the sealed classroom. They’re unusually well behaved today. Normally, a few would be out loitering.

Holding the faceless nurse’s uniform and the hammer, Chen Ge pushed the Third Sick Hall’s steel door open.

The Third Sick Hall is still unfinished, and its hidden mission hasn’t been triggered. At most, the scenario is fifty percent complete, so it doesn’t count as a true three-star scenario. With so many professionals in the group, they might actually clear it.Chen Ge walked at an unhurried pace. First, I need to find that madwoman’s mannequin and test this nurse’s uniform.

Chen Ge rounded the first corner and stopped dead. More than twenty mannequins lay across the middle of the corridor, blocking the way while their detached heads rolled from side to side. They appeared to be having a wonderful time.

“Why are all of you here?” Chen Ge stepped into the corridor, and the rolling heads immediately went still. Every mannequin began playing dead. “Is this your scenario? Why did you come to the mental hospital in your school uniforms?”

Naturally, the mannequins said nothing. They froze like primary school students caught by their teacher at an arcade.

“It’s bad enough that you wandered over here, but you let yourselves get dismembered too?” Chen Ge sounded angry, yet he felt sorry for them. He collected the heads from the floor and returned them to their owners. “These visitors wouldn’t even spare harmless mannequins. How cruel.”

The darkness made the work slow. After repairing the sixth mannequin, he stood and announced, “Once I’ve sent the visitors out, I’ll come back for the rest of you.”

Anger edged his voice. Gripping the hammer, Chen Ge raced down the corridor.

…

Inside the electrotherapy room, Han Qiuming bent close to the recorder. He listened for a long while but heard nothing.

“Could the tape be blank?” It was the only explanation he could devise.

“Would the boss do something so pointless?” Ye Xiaoxin sensed there was more to the cassette, yet all she could hear was faint white noise. She tried the recorder’s buttons, but no matter what she pressed, the play button remained depressed and the tape kept turning.

“The boss must have modified it. These buttons are only for show, and the real power switch is hidden somewhere else.” Han Qiuming searched for a long time without finding it, and his expression darkened. Ever since entering the Third Sick Hall, he had tried to prove his usefulness, but its props seemed determined to contradict him.

“We should leave first.” Han Qiuming looked at his phone. “We have three minutes left. If we hurry, we should be able to make it.”

He left the room with Ye Xiaoxin, intending to escape through the secret passage in Room 3.

At the same time, at the other end of the corridor…

Guo Miao’s group rushed back into the depths of the Third Sick Hall. They searched the rooms along the second and third corridors, including the director’s office, but found no trace of Han Qiuming.

“Boss! We’ve looked through all the rooms, but there’s still no sign of Han Qiuming!” Song An exclaimed between hurried breaths.

“The corridors only lead one way. We should have run into him. Where did he go?” Guo Miao lightly slapped his cheeks. He had not felt this anxious in a decade. “Let me think. There are three possibilities. First, Han Qiuming found a hidden passage and entered it. Second, he hid in one of the rooms while we were searching, and he’s now deeper inside the Haunted House. And third...”

Gruesome images associated with mental hospitals flashed through his mind, and he could not bring himself to continue. He looked at Song An and saw his own fear reflected in the man’s eyes.

“This is bad!” The two men exchanged a meaningful look, making Su Luoluo’s scalp prickle.

“Do you guys want to continue this tour? Because I’m leaving!”

Her fear continued to mount. Even her fellow visitors behaved more professionally than these Haunted House employees, who would not stop saying terrifying things.

“No! You can’t leave alone—it’s too dangerous. We must stay together!” Song An ordered, as though disaster would befall Su Luoluo the moment she left them.

“Old Song is right. If we split up, they can pick us off one by one. As long as we stay together, the enemy won’t dare act recklessly.” Guo Miao forced a smile for Su Luoluo. “I’m sorry we dragged you into this, but don’t worry. We’ll get you out safely.”

Guo Miao’s apology nearly made Su Luoluo cry. Why are you suddenly apologizing? What is going on? You told me I was lucky to be chosen for this visit, but all I’ve done is run back and forth. Why are you doing this to me?

Su Luoluo began to suspect she had been tricked—that she was the only genuine visitor and everyone else was an actor. The two Haunted Houses must have conspired to frighten her.

“We don’t have time to waste. The longer we stay here, the more dangerous it is for Han Qiuming. We need to find him now!” Guo Miao decided. “Come on! Let’s move down the other corridor!”

He and Song An took the lead while Xiao Du brought up the rear. Before they moved on, Xiao Du told Su Luoluo, “Brother Song and Boss are reliable. With them here, nothing dangerous will happen to you.”

“What danger could possibly befall me inside a Haunted House? Is that supposed to comfort me?” Alone in a corridor covered with bloody writing, Su Luoluo reluctantly followed Guo Miao’s group. She did not dare return to the exit by herself. They reached the fourth corridor and searched all ten rooms, but still found no sign of Han Qiuming.

“We’ve reached the end. Where is Han Qiuming?” Physically exhausted, Song An leaned against the wall.

“How can a living person simply disappear?” Guo Miao’s heart raced. He looked around and noticed that the writing on the walls had darkened.

“We must have overlooked something!” Guo Miao gripped Song An’s shoulder. “Every Haunted House has passages reserved for its workers. The Third Sick Hall should be no exception. Several of the sickrooms we checked had unusual layouts. I believe the passage is hidden in one of them.”

“Okay, we’ll go back to look together!”

Su Luoluo was exhausted from following them. She had never experienced a Haunted House like this. “I just ran all the way here, and now you’re running back again?”

“The staff passage—and Han Qiuming—should be inside one of those rooms.” Guo Miao looked at Su Luoluo with an intensity he had not shown in years. “Trust me. I’m not mistaken.”

…

Han Qiuming and Ye Xiaoxin emerged from the director’s office with the tape recorder. Its white noise had grown louder.

“Where are your teammates? I seem to hear running.” Ye Xiaoxin kept her distance from Han Qiuming.

“Ignore them. Let’s get out first.” With the tape recorder in his arms, Han Qiuming felt as though something were watching him. The skin on his back crawled.
